closures.observed_ui01_evidence: Eleven unapproved brand files ship inside the public web root of the production image and are publicly served. The UI-00 brand inventory recorded 7 approved assets, 1 deleted by authority and 11 marked present_unreferenced; all eleven (PNG.png and ten v1/ChatGPT Image PNG working files) existed in the production nginx image under /var/www/html/public/assets/brand and were served.
closures.root_cause: Working files were committed under `public/`, and no build or image stage filters unapproved assets out. `docker/nginx.Dockerfile` copies the whole `public` tree, so anything under it ships and is served by construction.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The defect is location, not content. The files are harmless drafts; what makes them a defect is that they sit inside the one directory the edge image publishes wholesale. Adding a deny rule at the edge would leave the bytes in the image and depend on a config nobody re-reads; moving them out of `public/` removes the exposure at its source.
closures.correct_fix: A NON-DESTRUCTIVE quarantine. All eleven files were moved with `git mv` into docs/brand/quarantine/ui01-asset-002/, preserving the v1/ subdirectory. `docs/` is never copied into the nginx image, so the bytes stay reviewable and reversible while being unreachable over HTTP. Every hash was verified against the UI-00 inventory BEFORE the move and re-verified from the archived bytes after it. config/brand-asset-quarantine.json is the reviewed decision record; the UI-00 inventory could not remain the authority because it is a live statement about the filesystem and now correctly reports zero unreferenced brand files.
closures.why_not_deleted: Deleting product-owner artwork is not UI-05's decision to make, and CLAUDE.md §9 requires asking before deleting any data. A quarantine closes the defect and leaves the decision reversible.

closures.found_by: Phase UI-05, while defining the FAQ parser against all eight source documents.
closures.observed_problem: Sixty Merchant Administrator FAQ questions never reached any surface. The runtime parser in resources/spa/src/content/markdown.ts accepted a question only at heading level two (`h[1].length === 2 && /^\d+\.\d+\s+/`), and merchant_administrator_faq.md writes 60 of its 196 questions at level three. Every other account writes all of its questions at level two, so the defect was invisible in seven of eight cases.
closures.root_cause: The parser encoded a FORMATTING convention (heading level) as if it were the semantic rule (dotted question numbering). Seven documents happened to satisfy both, so the wrong rule never failed a test.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: The source documents themselves define a question by its dotted numbering — `### 9.14 Does the preferred personnel fee…` is unambiguously a question, and it was dropped purely because of how many hashes precede it. Counting them proves it exactly: 136 at level two + 60 at level three = 196 questions in the file, against 136 compiled before the fix.
closures.correct_fix: Heading level was removed from the rule. A question is any heading whose text begins with `N.M`; a level-one heading with a single number is a category divider and carries forward to the questions beneath it. Compilation moved from runtime to generation time, so the parse is checked in CI rather than re-run on every view.
tests: tests/Feature/Content/FaqContentContractTest.php — 'proves the sixty dropped Merchant Administrator questions are now compiled (UI05-FAQ-001)', plus a per-account completeness check that counts questions in the SOURCE rather than trusting the manifest
resources/spa/src/content/generatedContent.spec.ts — 'compiles questions written at any heading level (UI05-FAQ-001)'
closures.before: 136 of 196 Merchant Administrator questions compiled; 1,204 items across all eight accounts.
closures.after: 196 of 196 compiled; 1,264 items across all eight accounts.
closures.not_done_here: The public FAQ route that will render them is UI-06's. UI-05 supplies the compiled data and the SvFaq adapter only, so UI01-LEGAL-001 stays open.
closures.remaining_risk: None identified. The contract test counts questions in the source document, so a future parser regression fails rather than silently under-reporting.

closures.found_by: Phase UI-05, while replacing the image helpers with the curated manifest.
closures.observed_problem: `content/roleContent.ts` enumerated EVERY supplied image per role from a hard-coded IMAGE_COUNTS table (10, 8, 9, 8, 5, 6, 7, 8) and assumed `1.png` was always the hero. The authenticated role landing then rendered that assumed hero with invented alternative text (`${entry.label} working in Servana`) and declared width=800 height=600 for files that are actually 1672×941 or 1448×1086.
closures.root_cause: Three assumptions stood in for measurements: that a directory's contents can be derived from a constant, that file order encodes meaning, and that a generic sentence is adequate alternative text.
closures.why_this_is_the_root_cause: Each assumption fails independently. A hard-coded count silently lies the moment a directory changes; `1.png` is the hero by convention only; and the declared 800×600 against a 1672×941 file mis-reserves layout space, which is a CLS defect as well as a correctness one. UI/UX plan §8.7 also forbids rendering every image merely because it exists.
closures.correct_fix: Both helpers now read the generated manifest. `landingImages()` returns the curated selection; `heroImage()` returns the manifest's hero or null. RoleLandingScaffold renders a <picture> with the AVIF and WebP candidates, the curated alternative text, the file's real intrinsic dimensions, the recorded loading strategy and fetch priority, and the focal point as object-position.
tests: tests/Feature/Assets/LandingImageManifestContractTest.php — 9 tests including measured-versus-declared dimensions and the alt-text lint
resources/spa/src/content/generatedContent.spec.ts — the curated landing images describe block
closures.before: 61 images enumerated; hero assumed; alt text invented; dimensions declared 800×600 for every image.
closures.after: 32 images curated (4 per account); hero declared; alt text curated per image; dimensions measured from the files.
closures.not_done_here: Final image placement, cropping decisions and visual approval on the eight public landing pages are UI-06's; release_status stays pending_ui06_visual_review for every image.
closures.remaining_risk: The authenticated role landing is the only surface rendering a curated image today, so the responsive candidates are proven by contract and by the asset smoke rather than by a visual comparison. UI-16 owns visual baselines.

content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.observed: Four accounts supply a testimonials section containing customer evidence that cannot be published as-is. merchant_branch, merchant_finance and merchant_front_office each present an attributed customer quote with no verified source; merchant_personnel states in the source itself that its three quotes are suggestions to be replaced before launch.
content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.authority: UI/UX plan §8.4 — production must never display fabricated quotes, names, ratings, adoption statistics or performance improvements. The release has two acceptable states: verified evidence supplied and approved, or a product-owner-approved factual alternative making no customer claim.
content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.ui05_action: Compiled verbatim, flagged `renderPermitted: false` with an explicit restriction reason, and recorded in content-parity.json. Not rewritten, not deleted, not approved.
content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.why_not_fixed_here: Rewriting approved product-owner copy is forbidden (CLAUDE.md §9), and inventing a replacement would be exactly the fabrication §8.4 prohibits. Human Resource already occupies the same region with a factual trust statement and no customer claim, which is the approved-alternative state — so a precedent exists, but choosing it for the other four is a product decision.
content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.entry_condition: Verified customer evidence is supplied, or a factual alternative is approved for each of the four accounts.
content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.risk_if_ignored: UI-06 could render a fabricated testimonial in production. The `renderPermitted` flag prevents that by default.

content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.observed: Four of the sixteen plan regions have no source content: merchant_administrator, merchant_audit and super_administrator supply no testimonials section, and super_administrator supplies no pricing section.
content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.authority: UI/UX plan §8.3 (every landing page must preserve the sixteen semantic regions) and §8.5 (pricing must come from the role-specific landing content and the approved plan-price source — never invented tiers).
content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.ui05_action: Recorded as `missing_from_source` with `product_owner_content_decision_required` and owner UI-06 in content-parity.json.
content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.why_not_fixed_here: §8.3 states the IDE must not invent missing commercial or customer evidence, and §8.5 forbids generic Free/Basic/Pro/Enterprise tiers. Super Administrator is the platform owner's own account, so whether it should carry pricing at all is a product question, not a gap to fill.
content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.entry_condition: Approved copy is supplied for each region, or the product owner records that the region does not apply to that account.
content_findings_recorded_not_fixed.risk_if_ignored: UI-06 would either ship an empty region or invent copy.
